scope: throwaway probe package under plugin-packages/ (t1, removed on completion)

tasks.title: Verify the daimon accepts a loopback http:// URL (OQ-A)
tasks.detail: Probe with a SEPARATE throwaway package under plugin-packages/, not by editing the shipping generator — editing the generator to test it would put an unverified field into the package users have installed. Give the probe a single mcpServers entry pointing at http://localhost:8942/mcp, restart Kimi Desktop, and check whether the tool appears. Remove the probe afterwards.
tasks.verify: Kimi Desktop lists a prometheus-knowledge tool, or a recorded refusal

tasks.title: Determine whether the url form drives surreal-memory's legacy SSE transport
tasks.detail: surreal-memory answers GET /mcp/sse with an `event: endpoint` pointing at /mcp/messages?sessionId=... — a two-channel session transport. No vendor example exercises this. If the daimon cannot drive it, omit the server and record why.
tasks.verify: surreal-memory tools appear in Kimi Desktop, or an omission comment citing the probe

tasks.title: Investigate how vendor url-form servers authenticate before excluding forge-rs
tasks.detail: github and supabase are authenticated services declared with a bare url and no header field, so the daimon must supply credentials some other way — an OAuth flow, a per-plugin credential store, or interactive connect. Determine which before concluding a bearer-token server is unusable. Analyze raised this as an explicit suggestion and it was not acted on.
tasks.verify: documented mechanism, and a decision on whether forge-rs can use it

tasks.title: Resolve port hardcoding (OQ-B)
tasks.detail: Runs BEFORE t3 so the emitted URL form is decided once. Ports 23001/8942 are embedded; check whether they are user-configurable in the pack's own config. If so, read the value at generation time rather than hardcoding, so a reinstall on a machine with different ports still works (goal 4).
tasks.verify: either ports are read from config, or a comment records that they are fixed by contract

tasks.title: Emit mcpServers from the generator
tasks.detail: Add the mcpServers object to the manifest dict in the Python heredoc of install-kimi-desktop-plugin.sh. Include prometheus-knowledge; include surreal-memory only per t2; exclude forge-rs with a GENERATOR comment citing the 401 and the missing auth-header field. If t4 makes ports config-read, emit the resolved value rather than the literal localhost:8942.
tasks.verify: generated kimi.plugin.json contains the expected mcpServers keys

tasks.title: Regression: idempotence and payload
tasks.detail: Run the MODIFIED script directly first — bash scripts/install-kimi-desktop-plugin.sh — since that is what this change edits; install-skills-flat.sh only delegates to it and a green delegate run would not prove the generator works. Then delete the package and re-run install-skills-flat.sh to prove the wiring still restores it.
tasks.verify: direct generator run exits 0 and emits the expected manifest; after deletion the delegating installer restores 145 skills; no Mach-O binary in the package
